enumeration_note: One bidirectional Fibonacci pullback continuation strategy; the buy (uptrend) and sell (downtrend) sides are directional mirrors of the same skeleton, not opposing logic â€” enumerated as one strategy.

coaching_notes: You always need to enter the market in early stages of its trend otherwise you'll end up losing your trade
If you have identified the trend on its early stages then you can end up making huge profits from a single trend, because you just need to repeat the same process again and again
But if you'll follow each step carefully then the chances of loss are minimal
element_inventory: PRECONDITION: identify trend direction using a 4-hour timeframe + trend line before taking any trade
PRECONDITION: only trade in a trending market (no trades in a non-trending market)
Long entry (uptrend only): draw fib from swing low to recent swing high; enter buy when price touches the 50% or 61.8% level (anywhere between the two)
Long take profit: above the previous swing high
Long stop loss: below the swing low
Short entry (downtrend only): draw fib from swing high to recent swing low; enter sell when price touches the 50% or 61.8% level (anywhere between the two)
Short take profit: below the previous swing low
Short stop loss: above the swing high
strategies.entry_summary: Trend-continuation pullback using Fibonacci retracement on the 1-hour timeframe. First establish trend direction (4-hour timeframe + trend line). In an uptrend, draw the fib from swing low to recent swing high and enter a buy when price pulls back to touch the 50% or 61.8% level (enter anywhere between the two). In a downtrend, draw the fib from swing high to recent swing low and enter a sell when price pulls back to touch the 50% or 61.8% level. Only trade in a trending market.
strategies.exit_summary: For buys: take profit above the previous swing high, stop loss below the swing low. For sells: take profit below the previous swing low, stop loss above the swing high.
strategies.name: fibonacci_pullback_continuation
